editorialLexicalPolicy.evidenceBoundary: Spanish realization options and constraints only. These entries never override source surface, morphology, syntax, discourse, or canonical corpus evidence.
editorialLexicalPolicy.instruction: Preserve the bodily act and determine its relational force from the recipient and context. Adorar is permitted when genuine divine or idolatrous worship is expressed, but it is never an automatic gloss and must not make a human recipient divine.

spanishOptions.when: A divine or idolatrous recipient and the construction genuinely express religious worship.
The bodily gesture is foregrounded, including respect, submission, entreaty, or worship.
The act is directed to an authority or honored person without presenting that recipient as divine.

avoid: using adorar as an automatic gloss
inferring solely from the verb that the recipient is divine
reducing genuine worship to a merely physical gesture when the context establishes worship

editorialLexicalPolicyReview.title: Adorar, postrarse, servir y rendir culto
editorialLexicalPolicyReview.summary: Canonical and contemporary usage applies bowing and prostration to God, idols, rulers, relatives, and honored persons; recipient and context determine the Spanish relation.
